news.headline: Hormuz Disruption Drags On — Iran Demands US Sanctions Relief Before Reopening
news.what_happened: Iran's 2026 war has caused near-total closure of the Strait of Hormuz (20% of global oil trade). Iran's FM says Hormuz won't reopen until Washington eases sanctions and pays war reparations. IEA calls it the largest supply disruption in oil market history. Brent holds at $98, WTI at $90.
news.why_it_matters: India imports ~85% of crude requirements; diverting supply via alternate routes incurs a freight premium. ONGC and domestic upstream benefit from elevated realization at $90+ WTI. Airlines, paints, tyres and auto OEMs face prolonged elevated input costs. OMC margins squeezed as procurement costs stay high.

news.headline: RBI Rate Hike Expected Oct 7 — India Short-Term Yields Surge Sharply
news.what_happened: Bloomberg reports India Inc. faces higher borrowing costs as short-term bond yields surge ahead of the Oct 7–9 MPC meeting. Market is pricing in a rate hike.
news.why_it_matters: A rate hike compresses bank NIMs short-term, raises EMI burden, and dampens housing demand. All rate-sensitive sectors (banks, NBFCs, real estate) face a headwind into next week.

news.headline: FII Net Sell ₹10,148 Cr on Sep 30 — CY2026 Outflows at Record Pace
news.what_happened: Foreign institutional investors net sold ₹10,148 Cr on Sep 30 (Q2FY27 close). CY2026 YTD FII outflows are at a record pace. DIIs bought ₹11,272 Cr providing partial offset.
news.why_it_matters: Sustained FII selling compresses large-cap valuations. Nifty is already ~10.5% below December 2025 ATH of 86,159. DII buying provides a floor but cannot indefinitely offset FII pressure.

news.headline: India DFC 2,843 km Fully Operational — Railway Freight Loading Accelerates
news.what_happened: India's 2,843-km dedicated freight corridor network is now fully operational. Policy changes are shifting cargo to rail, with stronger loading growth in coal, iron ore and containerized freight.
news.why_it_matters: CONCOR (Container Corporation of India) is the primary operator on the DFC — directly benefits from faster transit times, higher throughput capacity, and lower fuel cost per TEU. Structural margin improvement.

news.headline: Nikkei +2.39% on BOJ; China and HK Markets Closed for Golden Week Oct 1–7
news.what_happened: Japan's Nikkei soared 2.39% after a Bank of Japan statement was interpreted positively. China and Hong Kong exchanges are closed through Oct 7 for National Day Golden Week holiday.
news.why_it_matters: Strong Nikkei signals Asia ex-China risk-on. Thin Asian liquidity with China absent. Indian metals stocks will trade without China demand cues for the entire week.

picks.catalyst: Hormuz disruption ongoing — Brent $98/bbl, WTI $90/bbl; Iran demands US concessions before reopening
picks.logic: ONGC is India's largest crude oil producer. Every $10 rise in Brent adds ~₹6,000–8,000 Cr/year to revenues. With Brent at $98 vs pre-war ~$70, realization is structurally elevated. Iran's demands (sanctions relief + war reparations) rule out a quick Hormuz resolution, keeping crude elevated for weeks. Stock corrected 1.83% yesterday providing an entry opportunity.
